classification.difficultyReason: Extract output per machinist per week, scale to the new workforce and divide the new production target by that output to find time.

content.prompt: A shirt manufacturer decides that he can supply 280 shirts in 4 weeks using 7 machinists. How long would it take for 15 machinists to produce 1000 shirts?

answer.short:
$6\frac{2}{3}$ weeks.

Find one machinist’s weekly output, then scale to 15 machinists.
answer.worked:
Assume each machinist works at the same constant rate.

Seven machinists produce 280 shirts in 4 weeks.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Weekly output of 7 machinists}&=280\div4=70\text{ shirts}\\\text{Weekly output of 1 machinist}&=70\div7=10\text{ shirts}\\\text{Weekly output of 15 machinists}&=10\times15=150\text{ shirts}\\\text{Time required}&=\frac{1000}{150}\text{ weeks}\\\text{Time required}&=\frac{20}{3}\text{ weeks}\\\text{Time required}&=6\frac{2}{3}\text{ weeks}\end{align*}$$
